subtopics.title: The skeletal system: bones and functions

outcomes.text: Name and locate the major bones from cranium and vertebrae to tarsals and metatarsals.
Explain how the skeleton gives support, posture, protection, movement, blood cell production and mineral storage, with sporting examples.
Define a synovial joint and name the hinge joints (knee, elbow) and ball and socket joints (shoulder, hip) with their articulating bones.
Describe flexion and extension at hinge joints.
Describe flexion, extension, rotation, abduction, adduction and circumduction at ball and socket joints.
State the roles of ligaments, cartilage and tendons.
Name and locate the major muscle groups and apply their use to sport.
Define agonist, antagonist and fixator and explain antagonistic muscle action.
Describe first, second and third class levers using neck, ankle and elbow, and define mechanical advantage.
Locate the frontal, transverse and sagittal planes of movement and apply them to sport.
Locate the frontal, transverse and longitudinal axes of rotation and apply them to sport.
Describe the double circulatory system, and arteries, capillaries and veins.
Trace blood through the heart: atria, ventricles, valves, septum and major vessels.
Define heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output, and state the role of red blood cells.

subtopics.title: The respiratory system and exercise types

outcomes.text: Trace air through mouth, nose, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli.
State the roles of the diaphragm and intercostals, and define breathing rate, tidal volume and minute ventilation.
Explain alveoli as the site of gas exchange.
Define aerobic and anaerobic exercise with sporting examples.
Explain short-term effects on muscle temperature, and heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output.
Explain redistribution of blood flow, and respiratory rate, tidal volume and minute ventilation.
Explain oxygen delivery to working muscles and lactic acid production.
Collect and use data on short-term effects of exercise.
Explain long-term effects on bone density, muscle hypertrophy, strength, endurance and resistance to fatigue.
Explain long-term effects on heart hypertrophy, resting heart rate and stroke volume, cardiac output and recovery rate.
Explain long-term effects on aerobic capacity, respiratory muscles, tidal and minute volume, and capillarisation.
Collect and use data on long-term effects of exercise.

subtopics.title: Components of fitness: endurance, speed and strength

outcomes.text: Define cardiovascular endurance, apply it to sport, and know the Cooper 12-minute run and multi-stage fitness tests.
Define muscular endurance, apply it, and know the press-up and sit-up tests.
Define speed, apply it, and know the 30 m sprint test.
Define strength, apply it, and know the grip dynamometer and 1RM tests.
Define power, apply it, and know the standing or vertical jump tests.

subtopics.title: Components of fitness: flexibility to reaction time

outcomes.text: Define flexibility, apply it, and know the sit and reach test.
Define agility, apply it, and know the Illinois agility test.
Define balance, apply it, and know the stork stand test.
Define co-ordination, apply it, and know the wall throw test.
Define reaction time, apply it, and know the reaction time ruler test.
Collect and use data on components of fitness.
Define specificity, overload, progression and reversibility and apply them to a training programme.
Define FITT (frequency, intensity, time, type) and apply it to a programme.
Define and exemplify continuous training, fartlek and interval training.
Define and exemplify circuit training, weight training, plyometrics and HIIT.
Describe the warm up: pulse raising, mobility, stretching, dynamic movements and skill rehearsal.
Explain the physical benefits of a warm up.
Describe the cool down: low intensity exercise and stretching.
Explain the physical benefits of a cool down.
Explain how injury risk is reduced using protective equipment, correct clothing and footwear, suitable competition level, safe lifting, and warm up and cool down.
Identify hazards in sports halls, fitness centres, playing fields, artificial outdoor areas and swimming pools.

subtopics.title: Participation in physical activity and sport

outcomes.text: Use current participation trends from sources such as Sport England, NGBs and DCMS.
Explain how age, gender, ethnicity, religion or culture and family affect participation.
Explain how education, time, cost, disability, access, discrimination, environment, media coverage and role models affect participation.
Explain strategies to improve participation: promotion, provision and access.
Describe how social, internet, TV and print media influence commercialisation.
Explain commercialisation and the golden triangle of sport, sponsorship and media.
Evaluate positive and negative effects of media and of sponsorship, with examples.

subtopics.title: Ethics, drugs and violence in sport

outcomes.text: Explain the value of sportsmanship and the reasons for gamesmanship and deviance.
Explain why performers use drugs, and the effects of anabolic steroids, beta blockers and stimulants.
Explain the impact of drug use on performers and on sport.
Explain the reasons for player violence with examples.
Define motor skills and the characteristics of skilful movement: efficient, pre-determined, co-ordinated, fluent and aesthetic.
Place skills on the simple-complex and open-closed continua and justify placement.
Explain goal setting for adherence, motivation and performance.
Apply the SMART principle to improve performance.
Describe imagery, mental rehearsal, selective attention and positive thinking.
Compare visual, verbal, manual and mechanical guidance, with advantages and disadvantages.
Compare intrinsic and extrinsic feedback, knowledge of performance and results, and positive and negative feedback.
Define health, fitness and well-being.
Explain physical benefits and sedentary lifestyle consequences: injury, CHD, blood pressure, bone density, obesity, type 2 diabetes, posture and fitness.
Explain emotional benefits: self-esteem, stress management and image.
Explain social benefits: friendship, belonging and avoiding loneliness.
Apply benefits to different age groups and respond to data on health, fitness and well-being.
Define a balanced diet and its components: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals, vitamins, fibre and water.
Explain the effect of diet and hydration on energy use in activity, with sporting examples.
